question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the exact solutions in radians to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x=0,$ for $-\pi \le x<\pi ,$ are

${x}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We divide each term of the equation by $\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and use the identity $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =0 \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =0 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x+\sqrt{3} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{tan}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{3}$ is inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3}.$

To generate the solutions, we add integer multiples of $\pi .$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\pi =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
